newsitem.title: USA: Iusacell CEO sees 35 pct sub growth in '97.
newsitem.headline: Iusacell CEO sees 35 pct sub growth in '97.

text.p: Mexican wireless company Grupo Iusacell expects the number of subscribers to increase more than 35 percent this year, president and chief executive Thomas Bartlett said Thursday.
"I do see that in 1997 we will be north of the 35 percent growth rate," he told a conference sponsored by Smith Barney.
Iusacell, the Mexican wireless investment of Bell Atlantic Corp, provided cellular service to about 250,000 customers as of March 31, an increase of 19 percent over the previous 12 months.
Iusacell had an increase of 17,000 customers in the first quarter "and I think you will be rather impressed with what we've done in the second quarter," Bartlett said. He declined to provide figures.
Iusacell holds four of nine cellular concessions in Mexico, with about 70 percent of Mexico's population.
The company also plans to install more than 60 cellular transmission sites this year, at a total cost of between $60 million and $65 million, Bartlett said.
Since Bell Atlantic assumed control in February, Iusacell has brought its product lines, such as paging and cellular services, into a single organization, he said. It also has raised prices twice.
Bartlett said Iusacell's strategy included bundling services and selling them at individual sites, as well as consolidation of its wireless brands.
Bell Atlantic owns 42 percent of Iusacall and has managing control. Mexico's Peralta family has 48 percent through Grupo Iusa and the rest is publicly traded.
